February, 1988       Page  Reply

     HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
     ----------------------

Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in  our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2 (Opus #4)
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length...

From: Dave Entwistle

Hi Ron & Brian,

I am half way through the fourth
edition of Outlet and find your
magazine to be the best thing
since Micronet.

One very minor suggestion, why
not let the cursor keys as on
the Speccy+ operate the pages
forward and back in addition to
the "f" & "b" keys?

It would also be easier to
operate the Jig-Blox puzzle if a
joystick could be incorporated -
Kempston style,to move the pixel
around and then the fire button
to move the squares.

Nevertheless, I will continue to
subscribe, cursor keys, joystick
or otherwise.

Regards and Good Luck,

Dave


From Brian to Dave

Thanks,Dave. We've taken up your
suggestion about the joystick.
LOAD JIG!BLOX and use BREAK. Put
this issue in Drive 1 and MERGE
*"M";1;"JIGJOY!".You can re-SAVE
JIG!BLOX if you wish by entering
RUN 9980 (This will  ERASE the
original so you may wish to use
another cartridge for safety).

Do you mean the cursor keys have
a page function on the Spectrum+
as on the old Spectrum they just
cursor up, down or along BASIC
lines? Which arrow does what or
are you talking about a program
in particular?

                   - Brian

From John Nicholls, Birmingham

Dear Brian and Ron,

Firstly, many thanks for issue 4
- the Christmas issue - which I
thoroughly enjoyed.

I regret to have to admit that I
have not made one iota of
progress with BONNABANNER as
yet. I am sure, however that the
help sheet which you kindly sent
me will enable me to make use of
the program in due course. It is
difficult to find the spare time
when distractions such as OUTLET
keep popping through the letter
box.

Thank you,too,for the assistance


which you gave me regarding
LASER GENIUS. I 'phoned Mr.
Mathews as you suggested, and
the result is that I now have a
working copy of the program. Mr.
Mathews was most cooperative.
Thank you, Mr M.

I was pleased to note that you
intend to expand OUTLET by means
of an extra cartridge or OPUS
disk. Please send me the extra
bit, preferably on disk. I have
not enclosed any cash, as I am
in credit with you, and I will
renew after six months - or
whatever - instead of 12, unless
there are any further changes.
No doubt you have computerised
accounts which cater for any
changes?

One such change which I would
like to see would be for OUTLET
to be produced on tape, as was
suggested in the last issue.
This would enable you to spread
yourselves out a bit more, for
you must find 100K to be very
limiting. Even the OPUS disk
can, so far as I know, only be
formatted to about 190K. I think
I did read about the possibility
of formatting to 512K, but I may
have mis-read it. I don't think
it would be very reliable,
anyway.

If you do go over to tape,
perhaps you could incorporate
some fast way of transferring to
cartridge or disk for those who
would like it.

I must take his opportunity of
saying how much I have enjoyed
all issues of OUTLET to date.
Obviously, not all programs are
to my taste, and I would like
to see more of some and less of
others. Overall, however, I
think you have probably struck
the right balance to appeal to a
wide range of tastes.

Well done, Brian and Ron!!

Merry Christmas to you both,
and may 1988 see you go from
strength to strength.

Wishing you all the best,

             John E. Nicholls

From Brian to John Nicholls

Glad to help, John.

There are many difficulties with
producing a cassette version of
OUTLET.Duplication would have to
be by a duplicating company and
it's doubtful they could supply
copies within the few days from
the last news item at the end of
the month to the issue of OUTLET
at the start of the next month.

The taped OUTLET would still be
limited to the size of the disc
version or it would just become
a different magazine.

What about cost? We charge `2
for the actual magazine, and the


cassette is about 50p, add the
duplicating cost and postage and
you're nearing `3 anyway - the
disc version is only `3.50!

I wish we could find a practical
way of producing OUTLET on tape
as it would increase the market.
Still, never say never.

It might be possible to produce
a stand-alone compilation every
few months of the best programs,
articles etc. without the news
items, letters and so on...

                  - Brian
[Look also at Ron's reply to Mr.
Abrahams (which has come to my
attention since writing the
above) on this same subject]

FROM: Joe Southall  [edited for
                        length]
...I still have some  suspicions
of the long-term reliability  of
the system (microdrives) and am
vaguely thinking along the lines
of the +3 Disc. Since you also
are hoping to use this in the
future, it seems that you think
the same. Am I being unfair?

...with the appearance of the +3
would you think that there is
much future for the 128K or the
128K+2?I only learned last night
that it is possible to add a
microdrive to at least the 2nd
of these,but is there any way to
stretch the 87K availability of
the microdrive to approach 128K?
  Yours very sincerely,
                    Joe Southall

From Brian to Joe

Thanks Joe. We are now less than
hopeful about putting OUTLET on
the +3 as it may not be possible
to access 48K mode programs on
disc. I don't think the 128K is
manufactured anymore but I would
guess the 128K+2 will continue
for some time. You can increase
the capacity of cartridges (98-
106K) with megaformat utilities
and we hope to do a review of
one soon with a special offer!

I feel that, with the exception
of the keyboard,the 48K Spectrum
is reliable if it has lasted 6
months with no trouble, i.e. if
you didn't get a dodgy one in
the first place. I'd recommend

that you stick with your present
system for the time being.If any
of the keys stop responding then
MICROSNIPS (see OUTBOARD) sell
keyboards.If the microdrive gets
unreliable then replace it with
a 2nd-hand Opus Discovery(if you
can get one at about `90) or the
PLUS D Interface and disc drive
at `130. This is just a personal
view you understand.
                       - Brian

FROM: Frank Harrop

Dear Ron and Brian,

Many thanks for issue 4 of
Outlet - another excellent issue
full of interest. I like the
Calendar programme, and you may
like to note that for the
Brother M-1109 line 3130 needs
to be amended by in serting
19,38 and 57 for 32, 64, and 96
(line-width?) respectively.

Ian Beeby had a query regarding
using a full-size printer with
Masterfile - I have found that
the best answer is to get
Masterfile version 09 (or later)
and with it MF-print. This
version also permits 42 or 51

chrs. a line, and the printing
facilities really are quite
comprehensive, altho' they do
need patience and time to set
up! The point is that 09 will
load files from earlier versions
so you can use your old data -
you do not have all the effort
of re-entering.

As I mentioned earlier I am not
at my age (68) interested in
games, but I look forward to the
single version for January and
enclose `1 with this cartridge.

Many thanks both for your joint
efforts.
          Sincerely,

                   FRANK HARROP.

To Frank Harrop from Brian

Thanks for useful info, Frank.

I must look back at what I said
about cartridge B as I seem to
have misled people into seeing
it as a games cartridge whereas
it will have the same material
as the A cartridge except for:
1. the editorial, letters and
other topical text items need to
be on the A cartridge so that
readers without the B cartridge
will not lose touch. 2. Big
programs will fit better on "B"
but they may be of any type.
There are useful programs on "B"
as well as lighter, entertaining
software.
                   - Brian

Ref:MICRODRIVE DOCTOR + M/DOCTOR
- I have them both. I was going
to write when I saw the Pipeq
bit in Issue One but, well...
Anyway I enclose a copy of the
Sinclair Amateur Radio User
Group Newsletter of 24-9-86
which refers to the problem. For
interest the Pipeq program is
for hire, I see, from SOFT LINK
if anyone sends off for the
catalogue.

Anyway, very best wishes & a
Happy New Year.
                 Peter Cole


Thanks Peter. I have written to
SOFT LINK to see if the program
is still available.  - Brian

FROM: Chris Clayton

Dear Ron and Brian,

On this cartridge you should
find a JOTTER file with my
comments on WORDMASTER, and also
a short WORDMASTER file. The
printout it produces is also
enclosed. I find JOTTER slow to
use so I will use TASWORD to
communicate in future. Am I
doing it as you require?

I enclose a cheque for the
January B issue. Please use this
cartridge. I am sorry to see
that M/DRIVE DOCTOR is no longer
available as I find it very
useful and easy to use. However,
RAMDOS UTILITIES, by ROYBOT, is

also very good, it does many
(not all) of the same things and
has other features too. I think,
if I have understood it, it can
be used to make cartridges more
reliable in a way similar to
that which you describe.
It does not Format to around
100K though.

Best wishes for 1988 to all at
CHEZRON!
Yours, CHRIS. CLAYTON.


Yes, Tasword 2 files, formatted
to 32 columns saves me a lot of
hassle. Thanks for WORDMASTER
info which we'll use next(ish)
issue and I've put the FOR SALE
notice into OUTBOARD.
                  - BRIAN

FROM: Mike Haine

 Dear Ron, Many thanks for the
Dec.issue. It is good news to
hear that you are going over to
a 2 cart mag. Follows a few
comments which come to mind
after reading the letters etc.
  I am intrigued to know how you
compress text? Apart from coding
out spaces longer than 1 char
long, I cannot see how further
reduction can be achieved at all
easily. Graphics are a different
matter as they tend to contain a
lot of repeated chars.
 You mentioned the problem of
reformatting text.I have a bit
of code in this version of Tas.2
which cuts out the spaces from
col.32 to 64,so that the text is

then Spectrum compatible. In
fact it is really for converting
text written with the RH margin
at 40 cols. to convert the text
to Prestel Standard.
 Incidentally it goes with a
further routine which prints Tas
2 text out in 2 64 char. columns
on my Epson printer. You can
have these if any interest?
 On the subject of line lengths;
It would seem to me that there
is a lot to be said for aiming
at 40 cols. This would then be
Prestel compatible. The print
routines might be obtained from
the VTX5000? One would also have
the Prestel graphics!!!
  On suggestions for the MAG. It
could be worth considering what
special things could be done


because of the nature of the
preparation and distribution
system. One thought, it might
not be very difficult to supply
a Mag. with the contents
selected to suit the individual,
from a range of items (progs
texts etc.) These would be held
in a fast access disc store as
data files and any selection
could be chosen from a numbered
list and loaded on the cart.
for each customer. Precis could
be given to aid the choice .
What fun!      On the subject of
'subjects': I would like to see
an article on disc systems.
There must be many, like me who
use m'drives but are worried
about their becoming obsolete.
What do we do next? What are the


chars. of the various systems?
 Printers are another subject of
general interest. It would be
nice to see an article on the
different DMPs, especially
showing the difference in
control codes systems and how to
modify routines from one to any
other. This might be started off
by a questionnaire which would
be filled in by owners of the
different printers etc. We see a
lot of queries about screen
copying etc. This is very
relevant to OUTLOOK. I have
found it useful to have ones own
COPY routine which can then be
adapted to meet different jobs.
eg. I can print Prestel frames,
stored in RAM files, with 3
frames across an A4 sheet (12/

sheet in condensed mode) and
with full Pestel graphics.The
print speed is 40 seconds per
frame of 960 chars.,but this can
be doubled, with a slight loss
of quality, to 20 seconds per
frame.The same routine slightly
modified should print 'OUTLOOK'
with 16 pages on an A4 sheet at
a speed of about 15 secs/page!
It is of interest that COPY mode
is commonly used normal size and
double size chars., but this is
the only example I have come
across where the COPY is in
condensed mode.

 Mike Haine (Prestel 788832249).

From Brian To Mike Haine

I like these ideas - especially
the principle of each copy of
OUTLET being "customised" for
each individual. Sadly, it would
be more labour-intensive than
you think because OUTLET is not
just a collection of programs on
a disc or cartridge. It has a
complex structure which IN EVERY
ISSUE has to be tested and de-
bugged like one giant, mega-
program! I have seen clubs offer
public domain software on the
Atari ST which you choose from a
selection but there is no sense
of a "magazine"- you sort it out
yourself. I think it's a tribute
to OUTLET that nobody really
notices how smoothly everything

inter-reacts at the press of a
key.If you only knew the trouble
we go to...

Our text compressor uses the
unused ASCII codes from 0 to 25
and from 128 to 255 to encode a
vowel and following letter
together in one byte so for
example, "al" might be replaced
by CHR$ 195. There was just room
for 5 "tables" (one for each
lower case vowel)each holding
the codes for the 26 letters of
the alphabet.

Certainly send in any routines,
Mike and we'll try to include
them. Hopefully Ron will do a
review of his DISCIPLE when he
gets it and I could do the Opus

Discovery..There's a possibility
of 42 or 51 column text mode in
OUTLET(see HANDYWIDE in the next
issue!)

I looked again at your mbx and I
think the only thing not covered
by my reply and this letter is
to note your comment that you
also find JIG!BLOX a bit boring!

                - Brian

From John White

JOTTER seems a good idea so here
goes. Thank you for the OPUS
discs of OUTLET 001-3 and 004.
The opening graphics on both are
excellent and the snowstorm on
004 is well worth watching
through.

I wonder if any of your readers
have tried the Word Processor
"Specword" which was published
in the January, February & March
1987 issues of the sorely missed
"ZX COMPUTING MONTHLY". I should
like to have written to them
with my comments on this program
but they closed down too soon so
I am interested to know how
others fared. I found it very

good having some features not
found in Tasword 2, such as
lines of ANY length, many TAB
settings, block delete, a very
fast word/character search,
instant word count, page
numbering at top and/or bottom
and more printer options.

Specword also has a space-saving
feature in that empty lines in
the text are only 1 byte long
(CR)[carriage return=CHR$13] and
all lines end at CR, with no
"padding" of spaces to be saved.
What it lacks, however, are line
justification, line centering,
whole line display (obviously!)
and fast screen scrolling. I do
not know the later version(s) of
Tasword and these may include


some of the above Specword's
features.

I should like to know of any
Spreadsheet programs for the 48K
Spectrum, either complete or for
typing in. I have the time (and,
after Specword, the patience!)
to type anything, being 68 and
retired(?).

Does anyone know where to obtain
a 3.5" drive which will fit in
the OPUS case and become Drive
2? It seems such a shame that
there is an unused connector
there! Also, the OPUS manual
does not give details of the
joystick pin connection. I do
not normally require a joystick
but, having just been told off

for not having one for GULPMAN
and other games, I feel that it
should be easy to knock one up
with four micro-switches (and a
zapping button, of course!).

Probably due to the pressure to
produce the OPUS Issue 004 for
December, there was a slight
error on the disc in that the
XMAS LOAD ER called up CONTENTD
instead of CONTENTS. This list,
which I assume is obsolete and
was for the original December
issue, caused confusion on the
next item selection by calling
the wrong program. As you had
what was, to me, an Edit-Proof
line, I used the SDC of
Keighley's disc editing program

to change the D to an S on the
disc.
     Yours sincerely,
                     John White

P.S.And I never saw the top hat.
Too much driving snow, I expect!

I remember "SPECWORD" but was
too lazy to type it in! There's
a spreadsheet program called
OMNICALC 2 available from
MICROSNIPS (address in OUTBOARD)
at `14.95. XMAS LOAD ER is
SUPPOSED to load CONTENTD! If
you alter it back & let it run
you'll see the whole DEMO. The
CONTENTD page you saw is a dummy
& loads the next part if you
wait for the scrolling message
to end or press a key...
                      - BRIAN.

Another from John White!
             [edited for length]

I saw that Mr. Andrew Clapham
(Letters 003) seems to have a
problem very similar to one that
I have, namely,a faulty address.
I do not know the RAM Test
program referred to, neither do
I know of any socket numbering,
but it occurs to me that "Error
in Socket 7" could mean a fault
in IC7, one for the chips in the
first 16K of RAM (though this is
not in a socket!).

My problem is at address 45030
(bit 5).I have a circuit diagram
of the Spectrum, Issue 2, and,
assuming that bit 5 will be on
Data line 5, find that this line


is handled by IC20. If there
were sockets then perhaps this
would be "Socket 20" but my IC's
are soldered in, unfortunately!

I should be glad if someone
could confirm that IC20 is the
one to suspect, as I do not
relish finding that I have
unsoldered the wrong chip!

The chips used for the 32K RAM
extension are type 4532. I have
read in an excellent Spectrum
hardware book that these were
rejects of another type (my
local shop thinks 4164; same
connection) which Sinclair was
able to obtain, having either
the top or the bottom 32K still
OK and which were re-marked and

known as 4532-H or 4532-L. There
are links on the PCB, adjusted
for (H)igh or (L)ow type chips.
Perhaps I can try a 4164; after
finding the right place, of
course!
         Yours sincerely,
                    John White


Thanks, John and I'll try to put
your own RAM test program in a
future issue.        - Brian

Yet another from John White!

Thanks for another interesting
issue of OUTLET (January). I
have yet to solve a JIG!BLOX and
so will not give an opinion yet
on whether it is "boring" or
otherwise. Being somewhat
addicted to puzzles I intend to
solve one first.

Mr. E.M. Duffield's letter seems
to confirm what I thought about
the locations of the memory
expansion chips on the Spectrum
Issue 2 and I should be able to
proceed with the replacement of
the suspect IC20, as mentioned
in my earlier letter. My circuit
board is marked with the IC
circuit references, so the


identities of the Data lines
will be: Line 0 - IC15, Line 1 -
IC16, Line 2 - IC17, etc. up to
Line 7 - IC22, all in the
positions stated by Mr.
Duffield.

I was interested in the program
"LPROMPT", especially the use of
address 23681. My handbook, in
Chapter 25,  System Variables,
simply states "Not used"! The
addresses 23728 and 23729 are
similarly dismissed, so I wonder
what they do?

I rather like "OUT-TAKE03". It
is always interesting to see the
Spectrum doing things that
aren't in the book.
             Yours sincerely,
                   John White


From Brian to John White

Address 23681 was intended to be
the high byte of the address of
the next LPRINT position in the
printer buffer for the ZXprinter
but presumably was not needed by
the ROM routine which probably
just uses the low byte(in 23680)
as an offset.

We may never know what the plan
was for 23728 and 232729 - they
follow 30 bytes reserved for the
calculator and before the 2 byte
address of RAMTOP.This is a good
place to ask everyone NOT TO USE
23728/9 in CONTRIBUTED programs
if possible as we use them in
OUTLET! 23728 has the microdrive
number and 23279 holds a flag
for the "NEXT ITEM" - Brian

FROM: Graham Yates, Doncaster

Just a "jotting" to let you know
that I for one will be wanting
the B cartridge of OUTLET.

This is the first time I have
found the time & a reason to get
in touch so while I am writing
let me add my congratulations to
the both of you for the good you
have done for the SPECTRUM with
OUTLET.

As I am mainly a user of
commercial software I don't have
much to contribute to OUTLET but
one of the things I do find
useful (now that I am using my
microdrives more often since
OUTLET came on the scene) is to
format new cartridges several

times (well 5 actually) from
within a short BASIC program and
everyone should know how that is
done. I find cartridges more
reliable after doing this.

1 FOR N=1 TO 5 STEP 1
2 FORMAT "M";1;"blank"
3 CAT 1: NEXT N
   P.S. No originality claimed.

Lastly, although you have said
you can supply cartridges, could
you supply cartridge labels in
small quantities? I have seen
them advertised at about `4 a
hundred but I don't want a
hundred. Can you help?

      HAPPY CHRISTMAS & A
      SUCCESSFUL NEW YEAR,
                    - Graham

To: Graham Yates from Ron
Thanks for your order and your
tip about formatting new
cartridges. As you say, this
isn't original but it is well
worth re-stating.
With regard to labels, I've put
a few with your January issue of
OUTLET to keep you going. I am
just re-ordering stocks and will
see what the current prices are.
There are a number of areas in
which we could become involved
in supplying or distributing
hardware, software and
consumables (such as labels) but
we are reluctant to become too
involved at present as so much
of our energies are devoted to
producing OUTLET.However, labels
sounds an easy one so I'll come
back on this with some prices.

From: Brian Gaff

Re: JIG!BLOX, I got bored with
that some time ago in those tape
mags! However a new reader has
probably not seen it so it might
pay to slip one in from time to
time!Ideas? Charset Design comp?
or maybe one to get readers to

my cocktail program!

Might I point out that the line
delete program [DELINER] must

The 2 cart system worked very

well and, as I have 2 drives, I
never noticed the change at all!
I do note though that you have
more free space on the carts.
This is, I guess, due to you
trying to keep the OPUS & MDV

I like the TASWORD file viewer,
[BLAST IT!] it should work with

I hope to have a sample of the

It has got to be the cheapest I
have seen for the Speccy. When I
review it [On his bulletin board
- B.C.] I can let you have a

want? Everyone after all is not
equipped with a modem!

You might consider doing "An
Idiots Guide to Solving
Adventures" at some point! I
can't do 'em & would love to
know the trick! Oh, by the way,
the above ROMBO device works on
the +3 as well.
                 - Brian Gaff

TO: Brian Gaff from Brian Cavers

We'd be glad of a ROMBO review,
Brian. As for the space on the
cartridges - the main reason is
that Ron's new drives format up
to 106K (with MDOCTOR) leaving
more space - the actual program
code is only very slightly less
than before. We're not too happy
about the reliability of this
monster mega-format and are
looking for an alternative.

I believe it's safe to use the
printer buffer on the 128K in
48K mode which is all we use in
OUTLET.
                      - Brian

FROM: MR. R. ABRAHAMS

Dear RON AND BRIAN
                  Thank you  for
sending issue four of Outlet, it
gets better all the time,

   I would like to add my penny
worth to the letter from G.A.
Jenner, about putting outlet on
tape, as tape is one interface
that we all have it would enable
every body to take Outlet,
after all better take a long
time to load than not have it at
all.

   Also it would enable folk
like myself who have thought the
Spectrum worth upgrading to save
it on the disciple disc or any

other medium providing there are
no traps to prevent saving
it,and of course it would be
cheaper.

   My microdrive has now given
up the ghost so I now have to
borrow one to read Outlet.

   Carry on the good work but
please give this matter your
most urgent consideration.

       Yours faithfully,

           R. Abrahams

Since we continue to receive
accolades for OUTLET,I think you
should know that Brian's largely
responsible for producing the
magazine whilst I count the
money-plus I ensure that a blank
disc or cartridge goes out now
and again - just to keep you all
on your toes! So stand up and
take a bow Brian- Hip, Ray! Hip,
Ray!Hip,Ray! Right,that's enough
- get back to your keyboard and
start typing. Why have you got
your socks on? -There's a spare
Spectrum in the corner, get it
plugged in - if you use two

Now, on to the thorny problem of
producing a cassette version of
OUTLET.
1) If it was just a straight
copy of the magazine then it
would either crash or attempt to
load a file from disc or 'drive
each time a program loaded from
tape.
2) The Opus version of OUTLET is
now out, with the Disciple soon
to follow and, even without
sections being specific for the
different users, the magazine
is bound to differ slightly in
operation so this would mean
that, if we adopted the approach
in 1), we would still need
several different versions
(ultimately) of the cassette
copy.

3) An alternative would be to
produce a cassette-specific
version that would auto-load in
linear fashion like the old
16/48 magazine - but this
wouldn't solve your problem as,
obviously, the magazine wouldn't
run sensibly on disc or 'drive.
4) Cassette copying in our
situation is horrendously slow
and with the full-size magazine
now running at something like
178K we would have to send out
tape masters for professional
duplication. This raises the
additional problem how many to
produce - it would be too costly
to keep going back for a few
more and too costly to keep too
much cash tied up in unused
stock.

5) It seems to me that we need
to produce an OUTLET newcomers
cartridge/disc which would
contain -
a) A text file giving any
details required about OUTLET in
general.
b) A copy of our JOTTER program
so that all newcomers have got
some means of sending in letters
to us.
c) A copier program that would
dump everything from disc or
cartridge to tape.
d) Anything else that makes
sense to include.

The cruncher here, of course, is
the copier. The ideal candidate
is the Sinclair Copier (for
microdrive to tape copies) but,

as we have said before, although
this might now be considered as
freely available to anyone
wanting a copy, we would be
reluctant to make it available
through OUTLET without
permission (from whom?). The
ideal solution would be for us
to write our own version but,
although we know how to do this
in principal, there are so many
other pressures on our time that
it is difficult to see when we
could undertake such a project.

Anyhow, as you can see, we are
looking at different ideas and
if anyone wants to chuck in a
few suggestions, they will be
most welcome.
                       Ron.

поклонись, Brian — гип-гип, ура!
Гип-гип, ура! Гип-гип, ура!
Ладно, хватит — марш за
клавиатуру и давай печатай.
Ты чего до сих пор в носках? —
В углу стоит запасной Spectrum,
врубай его в сеть — если работать
с двух клавиатур, выдашь вдвое
больше — живее, за дело!! [Но
сегодня же вторник! По вторникам
меня должны кормить! — Brian]

А теперь к тернистому вопросу
выпуска кассетной версии OUTLET.
1) Если делать прямую копию
журнала, то при каждой загрузке
программы с ленты она либо
зависнет, либо попытается считать
файл с диска или микродрайва.
2) Версия OUTLET для Opus уже
вышла, скоро будет и для Disciple,
и даже если не делать разделы
чисто под конкретных
пользователей, в работе журнал
всё равно будет немного
отличаться. А значит, при подходе
из п. 1 нам всё равно (в итоге)
понадобится несколько разных
кассетных версий.

3) Другой вариант — сделать чисто
кассетную версию, которая будет
грузиться последовательно, как в
старом журнале 16/48, но это
не решит вашей проблемы:
очевидно, такой журнал нормально
не пойдёт ни на диске, ни на
микродрайве.
4) Тиражирование кассет в наших
условиях ужасно медленное, а при
нынешнем объёме журнала где-то в
178K нам пришлось бы отсылать
мастер-ленты на профессиональный
дубликаж. Отсюда встаёт вопрос:
сколько штук заказывать?
Дозаказывать по чуть-чуть
накладно, а морозить кучу денег
в нераспроданном тираже — и
того накладнее.

5) Мне кажется, нам нужно
выпустить картридж/диск для
новичков OUTLET, где будут:
а) Текстовый файл со всеми
подробностями об OUTLET в целом.
б) Копия нашей программы JOTTER,
чтобы у всех новичков была
возможность писать нам письма.
в) Программа-копировщик для
переноса всего с диска или
картриджа на ленту.
г) Всё прочее, что сочтём нужным
туда включить.

Главная загвоздка тут, конечно
же, копировщик. Идеальный
кандидат — Sinclair Copier (для
переноса с микродрайва на
ленту), но,

как мы уже говорили, хоть сейчас
его и можно считать общедоступным
для всех, кто хочет копию, мы бы
не рискнули распространять его
через OUTLET без разрешения (но
у кого его брать?). Идеальным
решением было бы написать
собственный копировщик, и в
теории мы знаем, как это сделать,
но из-за кучи других дел трудно
представить, когда мы сможем
взяться за такой проект.

Как видите, мы перебираем разные
идеи, и если у кого-то есть
толковые мысли на этот счёт —
милости просим, делитесь.
                       Ron.

ОТ: TOM ASHMORE, CAMARTHEN

Дорогой Ron!
Спасибо за весточку, присланную
вместе с двумя старыми номерами и
выпуском 004.

Да, на одном из картриджей,
отправленных мной и на который вы
записали выпуск 001, был материал.
Боюсь, этот картридж повреждён,
так как второй раз загрузить его
я уже не смог (звучит картридж
крайне нездорово!)

..Посылаю вам этот картридж в
надежде, что вы сперва сможете
прочесть это письмо и копию моего
предыдущего (да, я сохранил копию
— и на MDV, и на бумаге), а затем

сделать ещё одну копию Issue 001.
           Искренне ваш,
               Tom Ashmore

Моё предыдущее письмо:-

21 ноября 1987 г.
Редакции "OUTLET"

Уважаемые редакторы!
Спасибо, что прислали мой
первый номер "OUTLET" (выпуск
003).
Это показалось мне крайне
интересным, интригующим и
полезным. Главное, у "OUTLET"
очень дружелюбная, личная
атмосфера, совсем не такая,
как у бумажного журнала.
Поздравляю и желаю удачи!

Из приложенного бланка заказа
(Order Form) вы увидите, что я
хотел бы получить первые два
выпуска. Не сомневаюсь, что в
одном из них найду подробности
о программе Jotter, на которую
вы ссылаетесь в своем буклете.
(Для пользы новых подписчиков
было бы полезно включать эту
программу или упоминание о ней
в каждый номер.)

А теперь просьба о помощи!
Некоторые из моих картриджей MDV
содержат смесь типов файлов,
например: программы на BASIC,
массивы данных или CODE
(созданные через SAVE), а также
файлы данных от OPEN и PRINT.
Как мне узнать тип любого файла,
не пытаясь делать MOVE или LOAD
(& не дожидаясь сообщения об
ошибке "Wrong file type ")? Если

это программа на BASIC, как
узнать длину программы и номер
строки автозапуска? Если это
CODE, как найти начальный адрес
и количество байт?

По словам Mike James в его
отличной книге "An Expert Guide
to the Spectrum", Granada
Publishing, 1984 p 137,
информация о файле "non-PRINT"
находится в записи 0 этого файла.
Однако, похоже, невозможно
получить доступ к этой записи из
BASIC (& я не знаю ассемблера).
Знаете ли вы или кто-то из ваших
читателей процедуру, которая
могла бы прочитать запись 0?
        Искренне ваш,
           Tom Ashmore


ОТ: BRIAN ДЛЯ TOM ASHMORE

Спасибо, Tom, и думаю, что ты
прав насчет того, чтобы сообщать
новичкам о JOTTER. Можно было бы
поместить сообщение на первой
странице OUTLETTERS... Погоди...
Черкну заметку... Готово!
Недолго ведь, правда?

Твоя проблема с типами файлов
делится на 2 части: легкое
опознание в момент загрузки и
получение сведений о коде и т.д.
ЕДИНСТВЕННЫЙ СПОСОБ сразу понять
тип файла, на который смотришь
в CAT — давать ему имя особого
вида при сохранении. Изменение
ВСЕХ имеющихся файлов может
оказаться колоссальной работой,

но определенно стоит начать
прямо сейчас со всех НОВЫХ
файлов, придерживаться системы
и постепенно менять старые файлы,
КОТОРЫЕ ТЫ ИСПОЛЬЗУЕШЬ ЧАЩЕ
ВСЕГО. Через пару месяцев ты,
скорее всего, обнаружишь, что
типы 90% файлов, к которым ты
обращаешься, легко опознаются.

Если почитать письмо John Luby
(если удастся втиснуть его в
этот номер, и оно будет не в
OUTLETTERS, а отдельным пунктом
в CONTENTS), ты увидишь отличный
список суффиксов, которые можно
добавлять к именам программ для
определения их типа. Как и John,
я сам пишу заглавными буквами
без суффикса для всех программ
BASIC, но использую синклеровские

суффиксы-токены вроде CODE
или DATA в конце строчных имен
для прочих файлов. Это оставляет
целых 9 символов под имя, но,
как отмечает John, означает, что
нельзя будет использовать
загрузчик с меню, "читающий" имя
файла с экрана через SCREEN$, так
как он прочитает, например,
токен CODE как четыре буквы.
Впрочем, я никогда не пользуюсь
таким загрузчиком, так что бе-бе-
бе John Luby! К тому же мне лично
"удобно" постоянно использовать
токены. Ты должен сам решить,
какую систему использовать (и
нужна ли она вообще), ведь это
чисто дело личного вкуса.

Что касается получения сведений
о файлах, существует несколько

программ "расширенного CAT".
У меня есть MDOCTOR, и я пытаюсь
выяснить, продается ли она еще
(она защищена копирайтом, так что
я не могу поместить ее в OUTLET).
Последний час я перерывал
рекламные объявления в поисках
других подобных программ, но пока
безуспешно. Уверен, что доступна
хотя бы парочка, и я постараюсь
дать информацию в следующем
OUTLET. В любом случае, это
кажется хорошим проектом для
разработки утилиты для OUTLET, но
это может занять время... Я
посмотрю, что можно сделать.
                              - Brian.

### HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET

Letters are accepted in almost any form for publication in our OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or DATA statements, handwritten or typed pages, a simple JOTTER program is provided in Issue 2 (Opus #4) mailbox messages via Prestel No. 014703943 but the easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length...

### From: Dave Entwistle

Hi Ron & Brian,

I am half way through the fourth edition of Outlet and find your magazine to be the best thing since Micronet.

One very minor suggestion, why not let the cursor keys as on the Speccy+ operate the pages forward and back in addition to the "f" & "b" keys?

It would also be easier to operate the Jig-Blox puzzle if a joystick could be incorporated - Kempston style, to move the pixel around and then the fire button to move the squares.

Nevertheless, I will continue to subscribe, cursor keys, joystick or otherwise.

Regards and Good Luck,  
Dave

#### From Brian to Dave

Thanks, Dave. We've taken up your suggestion about the joystick. LOAD JIG!BLOX and use BREAK. Put this issue in Drive 1 and MERGE *"M";1;"JIGJOY!". You can re-SAVE JIG!BLOX if you wish by entering RUN 9980 (This will ERASE the original so you may wish to use another cartridge for safety).

Do you mean the cursor keys have a page function on the Spectrum+ as on the old Spectrum they just cursor up, down or along BASIC lines? Which arrow does what or are you talking about a program in particular?

\- Brian

### From John Nicholls, Birmingham

Dear Brian and Ron,

Firstly, many thanks for issue 4 - the Christmas issue - which I thoroughly enjoyed.

I regret to have to admit that I have not made one iota of progress with BONNABANNER as yet. I am sure, however that the help sheet which you kindly sent me will enable me to make use of the program in due course. It is difficult to find the spare time when distractions such as OUTLET keep popping through the letter box.

Thank you, too, for the assistance which you gave me regarding LASER GENIUS. I 'phoned Mr. Mathews as you suggested, and the result is that I now have a working copy of the program. Mr. Mathews was most cooperative. Thank you, Mr M.

I was pleased to note that you intend to expand OUTLET by means of an extra cartridge or OPUS disk. Please send me the extra bit, preferably on disk. I have not enclosed any cash, as I am in credit with you, and I will renew after six months - or whatever - instead of 12, unless there are any further changes. No doubt you have computerised accounts which cater for any changes?

One such change which I would like to see would be for OUTLET to be produced on tape, as was suggested in the last issue. This would enable you to spread yourselves out a bit more, for you must find 100K to be very limiting. Even the OPUS disk can, so far as I know, only be formatted to about 190K. I think I did read about the possibility of formatting to 512K, but I may have mis-read it. I don't think it would be very reliable, anyway.

If you do go over to tape, perhaps you could incorporate some fast way of transferring to cartridge or disk for those who would like it.

I must take his opportunity of saying how much I have enjoyed all issues of OUTLET to date. Obviously, not all programs are to my taste, and I would like to see more of some and less of others. Overall, however, I think you have probably struck the right balance to appeal to a wide range of tastes.

Well done, Brian and Ron!!

Merry Christmas to you both, and may 1988 see you go from strength to strength.

Wishing you all the best,  
John E. Nicholls

#### From Brian to John Nicholls

Glad to help, John.

There are many difficulties with producing a cassette version of OUTLET. Duplication would have to be by a duplicating company and it's doubtful they could supply copies within the few days from the last news item at the end of the month to the issue of OUTLET at the start of the next month.

The taped OUTLET would still be limited to the size of the disc version or it would just become a different magazine.

What about cost? We charge £2 for the actual magazine, and the cassette is about 50p, add the duplicating cost and postage and you're nearing £3 anyway - the disc version is only £3.50!

I wish we could find a practical way of producing OUTLET on tape as it would increase the market. Still, never say never.

It might be possible to produce a stand-alone compilation every few months of the best programs, articles etc. without the news items, letters and so on...

\- Brian

*[Look also at Ron's reply to Mr. Abrahams (which has come to my attention since writing the above) on this same subject]*

...I still have some suspicions of the long-term reliability of the system (microdrives) and am vaguely thinking along the lines of the +3 Disc. Since you also are hoping to use this in the future, it seems that you think the same. Am I being unfair?

Yours very sincerely,

### From Brian to Joe

Thanks Joe. We are now less than hopeful about putting OUTLET on the +3 as it may not be possible to access 48K mode programs on disc. I don't think the 128K is manufactured anymore but I would guess the 128K+2 will continue for some time. You can increase the capacity of cartridges (98-106K) with megaformat utilities and we hope to do a review of one soon with a special offer!

I feel that, with the exception of the keyboard, the 48K Spectrum is reliable if it has lasted 6 months with no trouble, i.e. if you didn't get a dodgy one in the first place. I'd recommend that you stick with your present system for the time being. If any of the keys stop responding then MICROSNIPS (see OUTBOARD) sell keyboards. If the microdrive gets unreliable then replace it with a 2nd-hand Opus Discovery (if you can get one at about £90) or the PLUS D Interface and disc drive at £130. This is just a personal view you understand.

— Brian

### FROM: Frank Harrop

Dear Ron and Brian,

Many thanks for issue 4 of Outlet — another excellent issue full of interest. I like the Calendar programme, and you may like to note that for the Brother M-1109 line 3130 needs to be amended by inserting 19, 38 and 57 for 32, 64, and 96 (line-width?) respectively.

### FROM: Mike Haine

Dear Ron,

Many thanks for the Dec. issue. It is good news to hear that you are going over to a 2 cart mag. Follows a few comments which come to mind after reading the letters etc.

I am intrigued to know how you compress text? Apart from coding out spaces longer than 1 char long, I cannot see how further reduction can be achieved at all easily. Graphics are a different matter as they tend to contain a lot of repeated chars.

You mentioned the problem of reformatting text. I have a bit of code in this version of Tas. 2 which cuts out the spaces from col. 32 to 64, so that the text is then Spectrum compatible. In fact it is really for converting text written with the RH margin at 40 cols. to convert the text to Prestel Standard.

Incidentally it goes with a further routine which prints Tas 2 text out in 2 64 char. columns on my Epson printer. You can have these if any interest?

On the subject of line lengths; It would seem to me that there is a lot to be said for aiming at 40 cols. This would then be Prestel compatible. The print routines might be obtained from the VTX5000? One would also have the Prestel graphics!!!

On suggestions for the MAG. It could be worth considering what special things could be done

because of the nature of the preparation and distribution system. One thought, it might not be very difficult to supply a Mag. with the contents selected to suit the individual, from a range of items (progs texts etc.) These would be held in a fast access disc store as data files and any selection could be chosen from a numbered list and loaded on the cart. for each customer. Precis could be given to aid the choice. What fun!

On the subject of 'subjects': I would like to see an article on disc systems. There must be many, like me who use m'drives but are worried about their becoming obsolete. What do we do next? What are the chars. of the various systems?

Printers are another subject of general interest. It would be nice to see an article on the different DMPs, especially showing the difference in control codes systems and how to modify routines from one to any other. This might be started off by a questionnaire which would be filled in by owners of the different printers etc. We see a lot of queries about screen copying etc. This is very relevant to OUTLOOK. I have found it useful to have ones own COPY routine which can then be adapted to meet different jobs. eg. I can print Prestel frames, stored in RAM files, with 3 frames across an A4 sheet (12/sheet in condensed mode) and with full Prestel graphics. The print speed is 40 seconds per frame of 960 chars., but this can be doubled, with a slight loss of quality, to 20 seconds per frame. The same routine slightly modified should print 'OUTLOOK' with 16 pages on an A4 sheet at a speed of about 15 secs/page! It is of interest that COPY mode is commonly used normal size and double size chars., but this is the only example I have come across where the COPY is in condensed mode.

Mike Haine (Prestel 788832249).

PS adding times!

```basic

 10 INPUT "mins? ";m;"secs?  ";s:let tot= tot +60 * m + s :PRINT "TOTAL= "; INT (tot/60);"mins."; tot - INT(tot/60); "secs". GOTO 10
```

### From Brian To Mike Haine

I like these ideas — especially the principle of each copy of OUTLET being "customised" for each individual. Sadly, it would be more labour-intensive than you think because OUTLET is not just a collection of programs on a disc or cartridge. It has a complex structure which IN EVERY ISSUE has to be tested and de-bugged like one giant, mega-program! I have seen clubs offer public domain software on the Atari ST which you choose from a selection but there is no sense of a "magazine" — you sort it out yourself. I think it's a tribute to OUTLET that nobody really notices how smoothly everything inter-reacts at the press of a key. If you only knew the trouble we go to...

Our text compressor uses the unused ASCII codes from 0 to 25 and from 128 to 255 to encode a vowel and following letter together in one byte so for example, "al" might be replaced by CHR$ 195. There was just room for 5 "tables" (one for each lower case vowel) each holding the codes for the 26 letters of the alphabet.

Certainly send in any routines, Mike and we'll try to include them. Hopefully Ron will do a review of his DISCIPLE when he gets it and I could do the Opus Discovery.. There's a possibility of 42 or 51 column text mode in OUTLET (see HANDYWIDE in the next issue!)

I looked again at your mbx and I think the only thing not covered by my reply and this letter is to note your comment that you also find JIG!BLOX a bit boring!

\- Brian

### From John White

JOTTER seems a good idea so here goes. Thank you for the OPUS discs of OUTLET 001-3 and 004. The opening graphics on both are excellent and the snowstorm on 004 is well worth watching through.

I wonder if any of your readers have tried the Word Processor "Specword" which was published in the January, February & March 1987 issues of the sorely missed "ZX COMPUTING MONTHLY". I should like to have written to them with my comments on this program but they closed down too soon so I am interested to know how others fared. I found it very good having some features not found in Tasword 2, such as lines of ANY length, many TAB settings, block delete, a very fast word/character search, instant word count, page numbering at top and/or bottom and more printer options.

Specword also has a space-saving feature in that empty lines in the text are only 1 byte long (CR) [carriage return=CHR$13] and all lines end at CR, with no "padding" of spaces to be saved. What it lacks, however, are line justification, line centering, whole line display (obviously!) and fast screen scrolling. I do not know the later version(s) of Tasword and these may include some of the above Specword's features.

I should like to know of any Spreadsheet programs for the 48K Spectrum, either complete or for typing in. I have the time (and, after Specword, the patience!) to type anything, being 68 and retired(?).

Address 23681 was intended to be the high byte of the address of the next LPRINT position in the printer buffer for the ZXprinter but presumably was not needed by the ROM routine which probably just uses the low byte (in 23680) as an offset.

## FROM: BRIAN TO TOM ASHMORE

Thanks, Tom and I think that you have made a good point about telling newcomers about JOTTER. It might be an idea to put a message on the front page of OUTLETTERS... Hang on... I'll make a note... There! Didn't take long did it?

Your file-types problem breaks into 2 parts: easy identification at the moment of loading and obtaining details of code etc. THE ONLY WAY to immediately tell the type of file you are looking at in a CAT is to give it a special type of name when you save it. It may be a massive job to alter ALL your present files but it is well worthwhile starting now with all NEW files and sticking to a system and gradually altering the old files THAT YOU MOST FREQUENTLY USE. After a few months you'll likely find that the file types of 90% of the files you are accessing are easily identified.

If you study John Luby's letter (if I can squeeze it in this issue and it will not be in OUTLETTERS but a separate item in CONTENTS) you will see an excellent list of suffixes you can add to your program names to identify their type. Like John, I myself use capital letters with no suffix for all BASIC programs but I use Sinclair keyword token suffixes like CODE or DATA at the end of lower case names for other files. This leaves a full 9 characters for the name but, as John says, will mean you can't use a menu loader that "reads" the file name off the screen using SCREEN$ as it will just read, for example, the token CODE as the four letters. However, I never use such a loader so nah nahdy nah to John Luby! I also feel "comfortable" using tokens all the time. You must decide for yourself what system, if any, you use as it's really a matter of individual taste.

As for obtaining details of files, there are several "extended CAT" programs about. I have MDOCTOR and I'm trying to find out if it's still available (it's copyright so I cannot put it in OUTLET). I've been sifting through adverts trying to find any other such programs for the last hour but with no luck so far. I'm certain there is at least one or two available and I'll try and put some info in the next OUTLET. Anyway, this seems like a good project to develop as an OUTLET utility but may take a while... I'll see what I can do.

- Brian.

Спасибо, Tom, и думаю, что ты прав насчет того, чтобы сообщать новичкам о JOTTER. Можно было бы поместить сообщение на первой странице OUTLETTERS... Погоди... Черкну заметку... Готово! Недолго ведь, правда?

Твоя проблема с типами файлов делится на 2 части: легкое опознание в момент загрузки и получение сведений о коде и т.д. ЕДИНСТВЕННЫЙ СПОСОБ сразу понять тип файла, на который смотришь в CAT — давать ему имя особого вида при сохранении. Изменение ВСЕХ имеющихся файлов может оказаться колоссальной работой, но определенно стоит начать прямо сейчас со всех НОВЫХ файлов, придерживаться системы и постепенно менять старые файлы, КОТОРЫЕ ТЫ ИСПОЛЬЗУЕШЬ ЧАЩЕ ВСЕГО. Через пару месяцев ты, скорее всего, обнаружишь, что типы 90% файлов, к которым ты обращаешься, легко опознаются.

Если почитать письмо John Luby (если удастся втиснуть его в этот номер, и оно будет не в OUTLETTERS, а отдельным пунктом в CONTENTS), ты увидишь отличный список суффиксов, которые можно добавлять к именам программ для определения их типа. Как и John, я сам пишу заглавными буквами без суффикса для всех программ BASIC, но использую синклеровские суффиксы-токены вроде CODE или DATA в конце строчных имен для прочих файлов. Это оставляет целых 9 символов под имя, но, как отмечает John, означает, что нельзя будет использовать загрузчик с меню, "читающий" имя файла с экрана через SCREEN$, так как он прочитает, например, токен CODE как четыре буквы. Впрочем, я никогда не пользуюсь таким загрузчиком, так что бе-бе-бе John Luby! К тому же мне лично "удобно" постоянно использовать токены. Ты должен сам решить, какую систему использовать (и нужна ли она вообще), ведь это чисто дело личного вкуса.

Что касается получения сведений о файлах, существует несколько программ "расширенного CAT". У меня есть MDOCTOR, и я пытаюсь выяснить, продается ли она еще (она защищена копирайтом, так что я не могу поместить ее в OUTLET). В любом случае, это кажется хорошим проектом для разработки утилиты для OUTLET, но это может занять время... Я посмотрю, что можно сделать.
